title: Metrics records (all sources)
description: Raw rows from metrics_raw as tables, not graphs: every imported source side by side. Filter by source or metric at the top; the records table keeps the 100 newest rows per source, so a chatty source can never push the quiet ones out of view.

list.name: source
list.label: Source
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT labels->>'source' FROM metrics_raw ORDER BY 1

list.name: metric_name
list.label: Metric
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT metric_name FROM metrics_raw ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Sources overview
panels.description: One row per imported source: how many records it has in the selected time range, how many distinct metrics, and the time span they cover.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  labels->>'source'        AS "Source",
  count(*)                 AS "Records",
  count(DISTINCT metric_name) AS "Metrics",
  min(time)                AS "Oldest",
  max(time)                AS "Newest"
FROM metrics_raw
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Records
panels.description: The raw metrics_raw rows themselves — time, source, metric, value and the full label set. Newest first, capped at the 100 newest rows per source so all sources stay visible even when one produces far more samples than the others.

targets.rawSql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT
    time                      AS t,
    labels->>'source'         AS src,
    metric_name               AS metric,
    value                     AS val,
    labels::text              AS lbls,
    row_number() OVER (
      PARTITION BY labels->>'source' ORDER BY time DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM metrics_raw
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
    AND labels->>'source' IN (${source:sqlstring})
    AND metric_name IN (${metric_name:sqlstring})
)
SELECT
  t     AS "Time",
  src   AS "Source",
  metric AS "Metric",
  val   AS "Value",
  lbls  AS "Labels"
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 100
ORDER BY t DESC
